references.text: The preceding description of the northern border includes Hazar-Enan, which is also mentioned in verse 10 as the starting point for the eastern border.
Ezekiel's vision of the land's borders also mentions Hazar-Enan as a boundary point, confirming its significance as a geographical landmark for Israel's territory.
Ezekiel again mentions Hazar-Enan in connection with the distribution of the land among the tribes, showing continuity in the border description from Numbers 4.
The continuation of the eastern border description from Shepham, demonstrating the geographical coherence of the boundary account.
